question: For fertilization to occur, which suitable part of the flower should the pollen grain reach?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Stigma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **stigma** is the topmost part of the pistil (female reproductive structure of the flower) where the **pollen grain lands for fertilization**. It plays a crucial role in the reproduction process of flowering plants.
 
• The stigma is often **sticky** or has a specialized surface to effectively trap and hold pollen grains during pollination.
 
• Once the pollen grain adheres to the stigma, it germinates and forms a **pollen tube**, which grows down the style to reach the ovary for fertilization.
 
• The stigma is part of the **carpel**, which includes the stigma, style, and ovary. Together, these structures form the female reproductive organ in flowers.
 
• Pollination—the transfer of pollen grains from the male anther to the female stigma—can occur through various agents, such as wind, water, insects, or animals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Parts of a Flower:**
 
 
• **Stigma:** The receptive tip of the carpel where pollen grains land during pollination.
 
• **Style:** A tube-like structure that connects the stigma to the ovary, allowing the pollen tube to grow towards the ovule.
 
• **Ovary:** The part of the carpel that contains ovules, which develop into seeds after fertilization.
 
• **Filament:** The stalk that supports the anther, part of the male reproductive structure.
 
• **Petals:** Brightly colored structures that attract pollinators to the flower.
 
• **Sepals:** The outermost parts of a flower that protect the developing bud.
 
 
 
• **Pollination Process:**
 
 
• **Self-pollination:** Pollen from the same flower or plant lands on its stigma.
 
• **Cross-pollination:** Pollen from one flower is transferred to the stigma of another flower, promoting genetic diversity.
 
• **Agents of Pollination:** Wind, water, insects (like bees and butterflies), and animals help transfer pollen grains.
 
 
 
• **Fertilization:**
 
 
• Once the pollen tube reaches the ovary, it releases **male gametes**, which fuse with the **female gamete** (egg cell) inside the ovule to form a zygote.
 
• After fertilization, the ovule develops into a **seed**, and the ovary matures into a **fruit**.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Flower Parts:**
 
 
• **Stigma:** Captures pollen grains for fertilization.
 
• **Filament:** Positions the anther for effective pollen dispersal.
 
• **Petals:** Attract pollinators through color and scent.
 
• **Sepals:** Protect the flower during its bud stage.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option 1 (Filament):** Incorrect, as the filament is part of the male reproductive structure and supports the anther where pollen is produced.
 
• **Option 2 (Stigma):** Correct, as it is the part where pollen grains land and germinate for fertilization to occur.
 
• **Option 3 (Petal):** Incorrect, as petals primarily serve to attract pollinators and do not directly participate in fertilization.
 
• **Option 4 (Sepal):** Incorrect, as sepals protect the flower bud and do not play a role in the fertilization process.
